name: Retinal OCT layer-surface segmentation with column-wise distributions and topology/smoothness constraints: He et al. 2021 FCRN (column softmax + soft-argmax + topology module), He et al. 2018/2019 topology-guaranteed S-Net/R-Net and boundary regression, graph-search CNN hybrids (CNN-GS), Xie/Wu constrained IPM (2022) and differentiable DP (DDP, 2022) layers
authors_org: Y. He, A. Carass, Y. Liu, B. Jedynak, S. Solomon, S. Saidha, P. Calabresi, J. Prince (Johns Hopkins IACL); H. Xie, Z. Pan, W. Xu, X. Wu et al. (University of Iowa); CNN-GS: L. Fang, S. Farsiu et al. (Duke)
year: 2017 (CNN-GS); 2018 (topology-guaranteed S-Net/R-Net, arXiv); 2019 (FCBR, MICCAI); 2021 (FCRN, MedIA vol. 68, 101856); 2022 (constrained IPM, Optics Express 30(2); DDP, arXiv 2210.06335)
venue_link: FCRN: Medical Image Analysis 68:101856, doi:10.1016/j.media.2020.101856 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33260113/, PMC7855873). FCBR: MICCAI 2019 (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-32239-7_14). Topology-guaranteed CNN: arXiv:1803.05120 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05120). DDP: arXiv:2210.06335 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06335). Constrained IPM: Optics Express 30(2):2453-2471, 2022 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35209385/); mutually interacting surfaces: arXiv:2007.01259.
code_availability: Only preprocessing/data reader public for He et al. (github.com/heyufan1995/oct_preprocess); no official FCRN training code found [uncertain]. No public code located for the DDP or IPM papers [uncertain]. All mechanisms are small (tens of lines) on top of an existing per-column softmax.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (MedIA 2021, MICCAI 2019, Optics Express 2022); DDP is an arXiv preprint. DDP full text read (method and tables extracted). FCRN read at abstract and secondary-description level (PMC full text was behind a bot check), so its exact topology-module formula and loss weights come from secondary descriptions.
extreme_summary: Retinal-layer networks output, for every A-scan column, a softmax over depth per surface and read the position with a differentiable soft-argmax (exactly our per-column softmax + expectation decode), then enforce anatomy inside the network: ordering between surfaces via non-negative ReLU increments and inter-column smoothness via a constrained differentiable DP or IPM layer. Reported gains of the in-network smoothness layer over plain soft-argmax are tiny on MASD (2.77 to 2.75 um, 1.90 to 1.88 um) and larger on Hausdorff/outlier metrics.
task_definition: For each column x of an OCT B-scan, predict the depth z_x(i) of N retinal surfaces (N=3 Duke AMD, N=9 JHU MS) from the image, with ordering z(i) <= z(i+1) and bounded column-to-column change.
inputs: The OCT B-scan intensity image (plus 7 image-gradient channels in the Iowa IPM/DDP models). No neighbour images, no known prefix. Our analogue: the 16-channel 345 MD-column x 400 TVT-level cost image.
target_parameterisation: Absolute depth per column per surface. He 2018 R-Net: non-negative layer thicknesses cumulatively summed into surfaces. IPM: per-column Gaussian (mu, sigma) surface cost. Our analogue: TVT offset per MD column relative to the anchor.
output_representation: Per-column, per-surface softmax over depth; point estimate by soft-argmax (expectation); after the topology module or DP layer, one smooth surface per layer (a path). No multi-hypothesis output.
architecture: FCRN: U-Net-style FCN -> per-surface (Z x X) logit map -> softmax along depth in every column -> soft-argmax gives sub-pixel positions -> topology module that rebuilds surface i as surface i-1 plus a ReLU (non-negative) increment [uncertain on exact form], plus an extra pixel-wise labelling branch for layers/lesions. Xie/Wu DDP: residual U-Net (24 base channels, 7 levels) with gradient input channels -> 1x1 conv head -> N x X x Z logits -> softmax per A-scan -> mu_x = expectation -> on-surface cost c(x,z) = -(z - mu_x)^2 -> constrained DP over columns with |z_x - z_(x-1)| <= delta_x (delta = eps + max training difference), max replaced by LogSumExp with temperature t, soft-argmax backtracking. IPM: per-column Gaussian (mu, sigma) costs -> primal-dual interior-point QP with surface-separation constraints, differentiated implicitly. CNN-GS (Fang 2017): CNN patch classifier producing boundary probability maps followed by classical non-differentiable graph search.
core_mechanism: (1) Treat surface localisation as per-column classification over depth and decode with the expectation: fully differentiable, sub-pixel, and supervisable with both CE on the distribution and L1 on the expectation (identical to our alignment CE + expectation loss). (2) Enforce structure by construction inside the forward pass instead of post hoc: ordering by ReLU-positive increments (topology can never be violated), smoothness by a hard slope bound inside a DP layer whose soft max/argmax makes it trainable end-to-end, so feature learning receives the gradient of the structured output.
training_objective: FCRN: cross-entropy between column softmax and ground-truth column distribution plus smooth-L1 on the soft-argmax / topology-module output, plus pixel-wise loss for the labelling branch [uncertain on weights and target smoothing]. DDP: multi-surface binary CE on column probabilities + L1 on the DDP output, pre-train without DDP and then fine-tune with it (2.9 s/batch Duke, 13 s/batch JHU). IPM: loss on IPM output + CE on column distributions.
decoding: Soft-argmax (expectation) per column, then topology module (FCRN), constrained soft DP with soft-argmax backtracking (DDP), or IPM QP (constrained least squares around the column means).
metric_consistent_decode: Soft-argmax alone is the RMSE-consistent mean. The structured stages are not: DDP/IPM build a unimodal quadratic cost -(z-mu)^2 around the column mean, discarding multimodality, then solve for a max-score path, i.e. a projection of the mean sequence onto a smoothness set. For band-confusion columns this is neither the posterior mean nor mode-aware; it only smooths the mean curve.
evidence_scope: Whole B-scan (all columns of one image) jointly; single image, no multi-image evidence.
prefix_conditioning: None; the DP start is unconstrained. For us the known heel TVT would be a hard DP start state (all mass at the known TVT in the last known column).
propose_vs_select: Single output. Not a candidate generator, although the soft (LogSumExp) forward pass of the DP could be sampled to give path hypotheses.
physical_constraints: Surface ordering (non-crossing) and bounded inter-column slope |z_x - z_(x-1)| <= delta; both hard.
dataset: JHU MS: 35 Spectralis macular scans (14 healthy, 21 MS), 49 B-scans of 128 x 1024 each, 9 surfaces. Duke DME (10 subjects). Duke AMD: 384 volumes (115 normal, 269 AMD), 51 B-scans of 512 x 361 around the fovea, 3 surfaces.
synthetic_to_real: Not applicable; all real, manually traced data; augmentation only (noise, flips).
metric_and_performance: JHU MS overall MASD: FCRN 2.83 um (as re-reported in the DDP paper), IPM 2.78, DDP 2.75, DDP-less ablation 2.77 um; He 2018 S-Net/R-Net 2.82 um vs graph-based AURA 2.83 um. Duke AMD: DDP total MASD 1.88 um vs same net without DDP 1.90 um and FCRN re-implementation 2.78 um; 95% HD Inter-RPEDC 6.53 (DDP) vs 6.59 (no DDP) vs 9.73 um (FCRN). DDP ablation on JHU: average-HD gains 1.5-16% per surface; authors note visible over-smoothing on some AMD cases.
comparability: Not numerically comparable (different domain, sub-pixel errors on clean images, no repeated structures). Qualitatively comparable: same output formulation; ablations show in-network smoothness mainly helps outliers/weak-evidence regions, analogous to our band-confusion regime but in a far less ambiguous problem.
validation_protocol: Fixed subject-level splits (JHU MS: train on last 6 HC + 9 MS by ID, test on the other 20; Duke AMD random 266/59/59 subjects). Single split, no seed variance reported; p-values computed over columns overstate significance.
inference_budget: Forward pass plus O(X * Z * delta) DP per surface; for us 345 columns x 400 levels x (2*delta+1) is milliseconds on GPU or CPU. Fits Kaggle/rig budget easily.
repeated_layers: Not addressed: retinal surfaces are distinct and ordered, so column posteriors are near-unimodal. The ordering trick depends on knowing which surface is which (fixed identity), which is precisely what is ambiguous for us. A slope-bounded DP can suppress an isolated wrong-band excursion shorter than the jump the slope bound forbids, but cannot fix a lateral that sits in the wrong band for its whole length. Reducing each column to a quadratic around its mean (DDP/IPM) would lock in blends instead of choosing a band.
drift: Not addressed. The He 2018 increment parameterisation (cumulative sum of predicted non-negative increments) is the analogue of predicting per-column dTVT and integrating from the heel, which would worsen drift through error accumulation unless tied back by absolute per-column evidence.
uncertainty_and_calibration: None reported; column distributions serve only as a differentiable route to the expectation. No reliability analysis.
where_to_use: (a) Loss/decoder level in experiments/arch/seq_NN_train.py and seq_NN_models.py: a trained, soft, slope-bounded DP (forward-backward) layer over the per-column log-posteriors with the known heel TVT as start state, i.e. the end-to-end version of the failed post-hoc continuity decode. (b) Post-hoc variant on saved posteriors already exists (posterior_fb_decode.py). (c) The CE + expectation-regression supervision is already in our loss; nothing to add there.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion in short excursions (blend / wrong_mode segments shorter than the lateral) and broad-hump noise; not drift.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already done: per-column softmax over 400 TVT levels + expectation decode (He's soft-argmax); smoothed alignment CE targets (alignment_exp_smooth_sigma 1.25, Laplace targets) + expectation regression loss (He's CE + smooth-L1); post-hoc forward-backward continuity decode (posterior_fb_decode.py, negative result on 155 holdout wells: smoothed 5.78 and forward 5.70 vs mean 5.47 ft, only 67/155 wells improved). Not done: (1) structure inside training, i.e. a differentiable slope-bounded DP whose output is supervised so the backbone learns column posteriors that are consistent along MD (DDP style, pretrain then fine-tune). Our continuity decode may have failed partly because the U-Net posterior was never trained to be consumed by a path model. (2) A hard prefix start state inside the network. (3) Ordering/topology between multiple surfaces has no direct analogue: we predict one surface (bit TVT); the only analogue would be jointly predicting several typewell marker horizons with non-crossing constraints, which the target does not require. Caution: DDP/IPM use a cost -(z - mu)^2 that collapses each column to its mean and is useless for band confusion; an adaptation must use the full log-posterior as emission, which makes it the B05 differentiable-alignment item rather than a new idea.
proposed_experiment: Low priority (subsumed by B05; the post-hoc version already lost). If run: E1 (training, one 150-epoch ConvNeXt run + control). Add aux head 'ddp' in experiments/arch/seq_NN_train.py: emissions = log_softmax of column logits (not the quadratic cost); transition = log-Gaussian in dTVT per 32 ft column, band-limited to |dTVT| <= 3x training max, sigma either fixed from training wells or predicted per well by a small MLP on trajectory features; start = delta at known heel TVT; soft forward-backward in log space giving smoothed marginals. Loss = L2 of the smoothed-marginal expectation vs truth on unknown columns, weight 0.1-0.3 as a new unet_loss_weights key (config in seq_NN_cfg.py); enable only after 60% of epochs (DDP paper's pretrain-then-finetune). Evaluate with seq_NN_holdout_eval.py: (i) unchanged per-column expectation (does the aux loss improve the backbone?), (ii) smoothed-marginal expectation, (iii) 50/50 blend. Two seeds per arm; accept only if pooled-RMSE gain on the 155 holdout wells exceeds the +-0.39 ft noise floor. Control: same config, aux weight 0.
implementation_effort: Medium: banded soft forward-backward over 345 x 400 is ~100 lines of PyTorch; log-space stability and masking of variable suffix lengths need care.
gpu_cost: Banded forward-backward adds ~345 x 400 x 25 ops per sample, negligible next to ConvNeXt; backprop memory through 345 steps is modest at small batch on 8 GB [uncertain]. One 150-epoch run plus control, a few hours each on the RTX 5060 [uncertain].
distillation_compatibility: Compatible: the DP is parameter-light; the FastViT student can reuse it, and KD can target raw column posteriors (as today) or DP-smoothed marginals.
error_correlation_with_ours: High: same backbone and evidence; the DP only redistributes mass along MD. Not a useful independent blend member.
risk: (1) The post-hoc forward-backward decode already lost (5.70-5.78 vs 5.47 ft), indicating the Markov smoothness prior conflicts with how errors arise (whole-lateral band commitment, not isolated excursions). (2) Retinal ablations show only ~0.02 um MASD gain: in-network smoothness fixes rare outliers in weak-contrast regions. (3) Mean-collapsing costs (DDP/IPM quadratic) would harden blends. (4) Over-smoothing reported by the DDP authors; laterals have real faults and dip changes where a slope bound is wrong. (5) Topology/ordering has no target in a single-surface problem.
notes: Main value is confirmation: our formulation is the retinal FCRN formulation, and the retinal community's extra step (structure in the network) is the B05 differentiable DP idea, with small reported gains in a much less ambiguous domain. The one transferable insight is to train the posterior jointly with the path model (pretrain, then fine-tune) instead of smoothing post hoc. He 2018's ReLU-increment construction is a clean way to encode hard monotone structure if a monotone quantity (e.g. relative geologic time) is ever predicted (see B07).
